data.description:
# Split `_ref_lock.py` — it is pinned at exactly the 800-LOC hard cap

## Why this exists

Discovered while fixing bug `freeborn-dizzy-raven` (ebee-e959-8015-4e02), whose fix had to
add two markers to `_NON_CAS_REJECT_MARKERS` in
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py`. The file was at **799** lines, and the
CI module-size gate hard-fails **any** `src/rebar` file over **800** (no allowlist).

So a two-line change did not fit. The bug fix landed by appending the markers in a single
`+=` statement (with the tuple re-annotated `tuple[str, ...]` in place, adding no line),
leaving the file at **exactly 800**. That is a correct fix but a spent margin: **the next
change to this module — of any size — cannot land without splitting it first.** This
ticket exists so the successor does not rediscover that the hard way, mid-fix.

## What I tried, and exactly why it failed

I attempted the split inside the bug fix and **reverted it**. Recording the two traps,
because neither is visible from reading the file:

1. **`rebar._engine` is not an importable package.** The obvious
   `from rebar._engine.rebar_reconciler._ref_lock_push import ...` fails at collection with
   `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'rebar._engine.rebar_reconciler';
   'rebar._engine' is not a package`. Reconciler modules load siblings through the
   custom `_loader.py` `lazy_load(<key>, "<file>.py")` seam — see how `_ref_lock` itself
   pulls `_advisory_lock` (`_advisory = lazy_load("rebar_reconciler_ref_lock_advisory",
   "_advisory_lock.py")`). Any split MUST go through that seam.

2. **Tests bind to module identity and to logger names.** Routing through `lazy_load` and
   injecting a `_core` back-reference still left 9 failures in
   `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_ref_lock_push_classification.py`, in two
   distinct flavours:
   - `monkeypatch.setattr(_ref_lock, "_git", ...)` no longer reached the moved
     `_push_lease_cas`, because the module object the test patches is not necessarily the
     same object the child resolves `_git` from (two loader keys ⇒ two module objects).
     Symptom: `test_transport_failures_stay_fail_closed[auth failed]` and `[dns failure]`.
   - `caplog` assertions are keyed to the `rebar_reconciler._ref_lock` logger, so moving a
     function moves its `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` and the log-evidence
     assertions stop matching. Symptom:
     `test_cas_mismatch_logs_the_stderr_that_justified_it`.

   Any split therefore has to decide deliberately: either keep emitting on the original
   logger name, or update the tests' expectations — and keep the patch point that tests
   already rely on resolvable.

## Recommended seam

The cluster at the tail of the file is the one that already forms a call graph among
itself, and it is the same seam the sibling `src/rebar/_store/push.py` split used
successfully (bug f61c → `push_classify.py`):

- `_PUSH_REJECT_MARKERS`, `_LEASE_MISMATCH_MARKER`, `_NON_CAS_REJECT_MARKERS`
- `_is_cas_mismatch_stderr`
- `_push_lease_cas`, `_push_cas`, `_push_delete_cas`

That is ~90 lines, so it needs a little more to clear the "never create files < 100 LOC"
floor — the module docstring explaining the CAS-vs-server-fault distinction (worth writing
down regardless; it is the subject of bugs 4afc and ebee) comfortably covers the gap.

Semantically it is a real unit: **"decide whether a rejected ref push means the lease
moved, and issue the lease pushes that ask the question."** That verdict is a claim about
concurrency — an operator reads "lease moved" as "a competing pass stole this lock" — so
isolating and documenting it has value beyond the line count.

The dependency is one-way in principle (`_ref_lock` → new module), but the moved
`_push_lease_cas` needs `_git` and `_REMOTE_TIMEOUT_SECS` back from `_ref_lock`. Resolve
that at **call time** (not import time) so there is no cycle and so the existing
`monkeypatch.setattr(_ref_lock, "_git", ...)` patch point keeps working — verify that
against trap 2 above rather than assuming it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py` is under the 800-LOC cap with
  real margin (target ≤ 720), and the new module is ≥ 100 LOC.
- [ ] AC2: `tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py` passes.
- [ ] AC3: `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_ref_lock_push_classification.py` passes
  **unchanged**, or any change to it is limited to logger-name expectations with the
  behavioural assertions untouched.
- [ ] AC4: A test proves `monkeypatch.setattr(_ref_lock, "_git", ...)` still intercepts the
  moved lease-push functions — i.e. the patch point survives the split.
- [ ] AC5: The CAS classification contract is unchanged: `stale info` stays conclusive, the
  subtractive veto markers still win, and ambiguity still fails closed (bugs 4afc, ebee).
- [ ] AC6: `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the complexity ratchet all pass with no new
  debt.
data.title: Split _ref_lock.py — pinned at exactly the 800-LOC hard cap, so the next change of any size cannot land
